facts.fact: Eleven of the forty have not yet self-named and have no name beside their fresh pages. The queen claims Chathu's forty pages as the crown's because they were written at her table, and says Neela holds them 'on loan'.
facts.why: needed because the outline has the queen refuse a charter that gives up the crown's right to the unbound members' pages, which ch 29 builds on.

facts.fact: Thilak supplies a clean crown leaf from the queen's green case and a cracked pot of plain clerk's ink and a chewed reed; the roll is laid on a board across two buckets by the well.
facts.why: needed because the outline requires a clean crown sheet and plain ink.

facts.fact: Usha writes her full birth name, Ushakumari, on the roll. Kandan signs with his village, Mathoor.
facts.why: consistent with F863 and F511; small signing detail.

facts.fact: Janu lights a plain sesame-oil lamp on the bottom step of the west stair beside the parrot newel at noon, and says she will light it every noon she is in the house.
facts.why: needed because the outline has Janu light the lamp at noon and leave it burning.
